starts without this one's messages.

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

description: Use when an ARC grid has markers and a prototype shape.

# ARC prototype stamping

Use this pattern when an ARC grid has a repeated background, several isolated same-color marker cells, and one compact non-background prototype shape.

1. Identify the background color, isolated markers, prototype bounding box, and prototype motif.
2. Infer the prototype's anchor relative to each marker. In the observed task, the marker occupied the prototype's center cell.
3. Copy the prototype's non-background cells around every marker with the same relative offsets. Treat prototype-background cells as transparent; preserve the destination background rather than stamping the prototype background.
4. Replace each marker with the prototype's center/anchor value; retain the original prototype if the pattern indicates it remains in place.
5. Some tasks use the prototype itself as a motif to clone wherever that exact colored-cell silhouette fits entirely on background cells, rather than singleton markers as anchors. Test this from demos: search translations of the prototype's non-background offsets over background-only cells, paint those cells with the prototype color, and keep the original. This applies to arbitrary motifs, not only straight lines: use every cell of the prototype color in its bounding box as the offsets, and require all those destination cells to be the background color. Do not require the prototype's background-colored cells to match; they are transparent. Paint the union of all valid translations, including overlapping placements, while preserving every non-background destination cell. For a straight 3-cell line prototype, this means every all-background translated run of length three. Be careful to use the demonstrated motif orientation and preserve all non-background cells.

7. Coordinate translation and motif orientation are easy to get wrong. Derive offsets directly from the colored prototype cells relative to its bounding-box top-left, then slide the shape through the grid at every in-bounds top-left. Validate the rule against the demo by comparing the union of predicted translated cells with exactly the cells that changed from background to motif color. This catches wrong offsets and wrong fill-color/background assumptions before applying it to a test.
6. Check all placements remain within grid bounds and don't overwrite unrelated structures, then submit the full output grid.

Observed example: a 3x3 motif was propagated centered on each singleton marker, with background-colored prototype cells transparent. Verify anchor and transparency from each new task's demo rather than assuming every prototype is centered.

## Enclosed-region fill variant
A different pattern uses a single color (e.g. 3) to draw one or more rectangular outlines/frames, with a second color appearing in the demo output. If the demo shows the second color filling the strictly interior cells of each completely enclosed frame while leaving its outline unchanged, fill the enclosed background cells of all such frames with that output color. Infer each cavity's bounds from its outline and preserve all other cells. Do not assume the cavity sizes match: one task can contain frames with differently sized interiors.
